summary: Describes an experimental way to run SNMP directly on Ethernet frames rather than on UDP and IP. It is meant for local network devices that support nothing above the MAC layer. It was replaced by RFC 4789.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 1089 describes an experimental way to send SNMP over Ethernet MAC framing instead of UDP/IP. It is aimed at local network elements that do not support protocols above the MAC sublayer, and was later replaced by RFC 4789.

questions: run snmp without udp or ip
how does snmp run over ethernet
what ethernet type value identifies snmp
subtitle: An experimental way to carry SNMP messages directly in Ethernet frames

tldr.problem: Some local network elements support Ethernet MAC framing but not the UDP/IP protocol stack normally used by SNMP.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC assigns an Ethernet Type value so an Ethernet frame can carry a standard SNMP message directly.
tldr.outcome: This experimental method was later replaced by RFC 4789.

today: RFC 1089 is Experimental and has been obsoleted by RFC 4789.

sections.title: Managing Devices Without UDP/IP
sections.content:
SNMP had been used to manage network elements that support the protocol stack through UDP. The RFC notes that some local network elements, such as repeaters and wiring concentrators, have addresses and programmable intelligence but do not support higher-layer protocols beyond the Ethernet MAC sublayer.

It describes using Ethernet framing as the transport for SNMP instead of the Internet UDP/IP stack. This is an experimental method for local-area-network elements.
sections.plainLanguage: Some network devices can send and receive Ethernet frames but do not run UDP or IP. This method carries management messages directly in those frames.

sections.title: SNMP in an Ethernet Frame
sections.content:
The Ethernet Type field value 33100, hexadecimal 814C, is assigned to SNMP. The data portion of a frame with that type contains a standard SNMP message as specified in RFC 1067.

The RFC changes the encapsulation, not the SNMP message itself. It describes this as continuing the style used for carrying protocol data over Ethernet.
sections.plainLanguage: The Ethernet type value tells the receiver that the frame's data contains an SNMP message. The message itself keeps its standard SNMP format.

sections.title: Scope and Status
sections.content:
The method is for LAN-based network elements that support no higher-layer protocol beyond the MAC sublayer. The RFC describes it as experimental and does not define a change to SNMP itself.

The unit metadata records RFC 4789 as the document that later obsoleted RFC 1089.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC proposes an experimental transport for local devices with only MAC-layer support. RFC 4789 later replaced it.
